description: Trunk: portal login as superadmin (qa-test-journeyhawk@phronex.com). All CC portal and API journeys inherit this session.

steps.description: Navigate to http://localhost:3002. Wait for the login page to load. Enter email 'qa-test-journeyhawk@phronex.com' and password 'QA_SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD' into the login form fields. Click the sign-in button. Wait for the portal dashboard to load — verify no 500 error and the sidebar is visible.

Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc. Verify the CC product section loads without a 500 error or blank white screen. Verify at least one CC sub-navigation item is visible (Dashboard, Content, Skills, Instance, Users, etc.). This confirms the CC product section is accessible for this superadmin account.

Save browser session: Call the browser_storage_state tool with filename set to the stateOutputPath (.tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json) to persist cookies and localStorage for downstream journeys. This step is critical — without it, all dependent journeys will fail to authenticate.

description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Navigate to CC dashboard, verify all tabs load without crash. Targets defect #238 (hasCustomKey infinite recursion).

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/dashboard. Wait for the page to fully load. Open browser console and check for uncaught errors — specifically look for 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' or 'hasCustomKey' which would indicate defect #238. Record any console errors.

Identify all tabs visible in the CC dashboard tab bar. For a superadmin account, expect: Overview, Analytics, Info & Connections, Sessions. Click the 'Overview' tab. Verify it renders content without a JavaScript crash — look for stat cards, metrics, or an informative empty state. A blank white screen or error boundary is a FAIL.

Click the 'Analytics' tab. Verify it renders without crash. Check browser console again for new uncaught errors. Verify at least one chart container or metric element is present, even if showing zero values.

Click the 'Info & Connections' tab. Verify the tab content renders — look for 'Platform Connections', 'Instance LLM Configuration', 'Widget Embed Code', or 'Recent Issues' sections. NOTE: React 19 ErrorBoundary may log a console.error when RecentIssues mounts (known React 19 concurrent mode fiber-state issue, defect #251, fixed via ErrorBoundary containment in commit 993083a). This console.error is EXPECTED and NOT a failure — the tab content must still be present. A blank white page or 'Something went wrong' fullscreen overlay is a FAIL. A contained 'Recent issues unavailable' fallback is a PASS.
Click the 'Sessions' tab. Verify it renders without crash. This superadmin-only tab should show recent widget sessions or an empty state. Verify the tab responds and does not show 'Access Denied'.

Final console check: open browser console and review errors accumulated across all 4 tab navigations. FAIL if any error contains 'hasCustomKey', 'Maximum call stack', or 'infinite' (defect #238). FAIL if any uncaught React error crashes a full tab (blank white screen or full-page error boundary). EXPECTED AND ACCEPTABLE: a single React ErrorBoundary console.error from the 'Info & Connections' tab related to 'Object.entries' or fiber state (defect #251 — contained by ErrorBoundary, not a page crash). The presence of this specific error with the tab still rendering content = PASS.

description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Verify Info & Connections tab renders correctly. Defect #251 (Object.entries(null) crash) is CONTAINED via ErrorBoundary (commits 993083a+20d1b69) — tab content must be visible even if RecentIssues shows fallback. Regression check: full tab blank or fullscreen error overlay = FAIL.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/dashboard. Click the 'Info & Connections' tab. Wait for the tab content to render (up to 5 seconds).

Verify the main Info & Connections content is visible. Look for: (a) 'Platform Connections' section with CC API URL and Admin Secret rows, OR (b) 'Instance LLM Configuration' section with at least one instance card. If a console.error fires referencing 'Object.entries' or React fiber state — this is the KNOWN AND CONTAINED defect #251 React 19 issue. The content sections above must still be present. If they are: PASS. If the entire tab is blank or shows a fullscreen error: FAIL (regression — ErrorBoundary no longer working).

Verify the LLM configuration section shows at least one instance (e.g. 'e2e-test-instance'). Each instance card should show a 'Master Key' or 'Custom Key' badge, an 'Edit Key' button, and a provider label. Click the 'Edit Key' button for any instance. Verify an input field appears for entering an Anthropic API key. Click 'Cancel'. Verify the input disappears.

Check the 'Recent Issues' section at the bottom. It should show either 'No issues in the last 7 days' badge OR a list of recent error entries OR the 'Recent issues unavailable' fallback (if ErrorBoundary caught the React 19 fiber error). All three outcomes are PASS — the fallback is expected. Only FAIL if no section renders at all.

description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Navigate to Users tab, verify flagged users display works. Targets defect #241 (is_flagged missing from SELECT).

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/users?instance=e2e-test-instance. Wait for the users list to load. Verify the page does not show a 500 error.

Check browser console for errors containing 'is_flagged', 'column', or 'UndefinedColumn' — defect #241 manifests as a SQL error because is_flagged is missing from the SELECT clause. If console shows a network error on the users fetch with a 500 status, inspect the response body for SQL-related error text.

If users are listed: verify each user row displays at minimum an identifier (email or anonymous ID) and does NOT show a raw 'undefined' or 'null' for the flagged status column. Look for a flag/badge icon or a 'Flagged' column — its presence confirms is_flagged is in the SELECT.

Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/all-users (superadmin cross-instance view). Verify this page loads without a 500 error. If it shows users, verify the flagged status indicator is visible here too. A crash on this page with a different error than #241 should be recorded as a new defect.

description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Navigate to Skills tab, verify list loads and actions pass correct skill ID. Targets defect #252 (undefined skill ID in delete/submit/preview).

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/skills?instance=e2e-test-instance. Wait for the skills page to load. Verify the page renders — either a list of skills or an empty state with a 'Browse Templates' CTA.

Open browser Network tab and filter for XHR/Fetch requests. Click 'Browse Templates' or 'Create from Template' button. Verify a GET request to /api/cc/api/v1/skills/templates returns 200 with a non-empty array. If the template list loads, select the first template and click 'Create'.

After skill creation: verify the new skill appears in the list. Inspect the skill row — look for action buttons (Delete, Submit, Preview). Click 'Delete' on the new skill. In the Network tab, verify the DELETE request URL contains a valid UUID skill_id (not 'undefined' or 'null'). Defect #252 sends DELETE /api/v1/skills/undefined — look for this exact URL pattern.

If the delete request contained 'undefined' instead of a UUID in the URL path, record as defect #252 STILL PRESENT. If the delete succeeded with a valid UUID, verify the skill is removed from the list. Clean up by confirming no test skills remain.

description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Navigate to Analytics tab, verify charts and data render without crash.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/dashboard. Click the 'Analytics' tab. Verify the tab activates and the analytics section renders without a JavaScript crash.

Look for analytics metrics: total sessions, total users, active users, messages count. Verify at least one metric container is rendered (even if values are zero). A completely blank section with no metric containers is a FAIL.

Look for chart/graph visualisations (Recharts SVG containers, canvas elements, or chart wrappers). If present, verify they render without corruption — no blank chart boxes, no 'Chart failed to load' error text. Check browser console for Recharts or chart-related errors.

If date range or time period filter controls are visible, change the selection (e.g., switch from 'Last 7 days' to 'Last 30 days'). Verify the analytics section responds — shows a loading state or updates data. A filter control that does nothing on change is a regression.

description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Navigate to Sessions tab, verify session list loads for superadmin.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/dashboard. Click the 'Sessions' tab. Verify the tab activates without a crash.

Verify the sessions section renders: either a table/list of recent chat sessions showing session_id, user identifier, timestamp, and message count — or an informative empty state ('No sessions yet'). An 'Access Denied' error for this superadmin account is a regression.

If sessions are listed: click the first session row to expand or navigate to session detail. Verify conversation messages are displayed with alternating user/assistant formatting. A session detail that shows only raw JSON or UUIDs with no formatted messages is a display failure.

description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Navigate to instance settings, verify config loads and form renders.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/instance?instance=e2e-test-instance. Verify the page loads with a settings form showing current configuration values. A blank page, 'Failed to load', or 500 error is a FAIL.

Verify the settings form contains editable fields: look for instance name, greeting message, persona description, fallback message, or assistant name. At least 3 editable fields must be visible. A form with all fields disabled or no fields at all is a regression.

Look for a 'Save' or 'Update' button. Verify it is present and not permanently disabled. Do NOT click it — this journey only verifies the page loads correctly. Check browser console for any errors during page load.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Full skill lifecycle — create from template, verify in list, submit for review, delete. Targets defects #239 (401 for superadmin) and #252 (undefined skill ID).

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/skills?instance=e2e-test-instance. Click 'Browse Templates' or 'Create from Template'. Verify the template list loads with at least one template showing name and description. If a 401 error occurs on the templates fetch, record as defect #239 STILL PRESENT.

Select the first template. If a customisation form appears, enter description 'JH-QA lifecycle test skill — safe to delete'. Click 'Create Skill' or the confirm button. Verify the API response is 201 Created (check Network tab). If 401 is returned for the POST /api/v1/skills/from-template, record as defect #239.

Verify the newly created skill appears in the skills list with status 'draft'. Record the skill name. Navigate away to http://localhost:3002/cc/dashboard, then back to http://localhost:3002/cc/skills?instance=e2e-test-instance. Verify the skill still appears — confirming persistence.

Locate the QA test skill in the list. Click 'Submit' or 'Submit for Review' on it. In the Network tab, verify the POST URL contains a valid UUID (not 'undefined'). Verify the response is 200 and the skill status changes to 'pending_review' or 'submitted'. If the URL contains 'undefined', defect #252 is present.

Click 'Delete' on the submitted QA test skill. Confirm the deletion in any confirmation dialog. Verify the DELETE request URL contains a valid UUID. Verify the skill is removed from the list. Final count of skills should match the count before this journey started.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Navigate to content, trigger URL ingest, wait for status, verify content appears.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/content?instance=e2e-test-instance. Verify the content/knowledge base page loads. Record the current number of content items or sources listed.

Look for an 'Add Content', 'Ingest URL', 'Crawl', or 'Add Source' button. Click it. If a URL input field appears, enter 'https://phronex.com/about' as the test URL. Submit the ingest request. Verify the request returns 200 or 202 (accepted for async processing).

After submitting, look for an ingest status indicator — a progress bar, 'Processing' badge, spinner, or a job status section. Wait up to 30 seconds for status to change from 'processing' to 'completed' or 'indexed'. If the page shows a job_id, record it.

Verify the ingestion result. Two acceptable outcomes: (A) SUCCESS: the ingested content appears in the content list with a human-readable source label (the URL 'phronex.com/about' or similar), and chunk count is > 0 if displayed. (B) SERVER CAPABILITY MISSING: if the error message says 'URL crawl is not available on this server' or 'Use file upload instead', this is an ACCEPTABLE outcome — it means the server (EC2) does not have crawl4ai installed, which is intentional (crawl4ai pulls 400MB browser binaries, excluded from EC2). In outcome B, verify the portal shows a clear user-facing error message (not a 500). FAIL only if: content is silently missing with no error shown, or an unhandled 500 error appears.
Clean up: if a delete option is available for the newly ingested content, remove it to avoid test data accumulation. Verify the content list returns to its original state.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Full lead form field CRUD — create, verify persistence, edit, delete. Targets defect #240 (deep-merge preserves deleted field).

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/lead-form?instance=e2e-test-instance (or the instance settings page with lead form section). Record the initial count of lead form fields.

Click 'Add Field' or 'New Field'. In the form that appears, enter: label = 'JH QA Test Field', type = 'text' (or first available field type), required = false. Click 'Save' or 'Add'. Verify the field appears in the list with label 'JH QA Test Field'.

Navigate away to http://localhost:3002/cc/dashboard, then return to the lead form page. Verify 'JH QA Test Field' persists after navigation — confirming the POST to /api/v1/instance/{instance_id}/lead-form-fields saved correctly.
Edit the field: click the edit icon on 'JH QA Test Field'. Change the label to 'JH QA Test Field Edited'. Save. Verify the list now shows the updated label.
Delete the field: click the delete/trash icon on 'JH QA Test Field Edited'. Confirm deletion. Verify the field disappears from the list. The field count should match the initial count from step 1.

CRITICAL for defect #240: navigate away and return to the lead form page. Verify 'JH QA Test Field Edited' does NOT reappear. If it reappears despite deletion, defect #240 is STILL PRESENT — the deep-merge is preserving the deleted field. Check the GET response in Network tab to confirm the field is absent from the API response.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Edit instance persona, save, navigate away, return, verify persistence.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/instance?instance=e2e-test-instance. Wait for the settings form to load. Identify a safe text field to modify — greeting message, assistant name, or persona description. Record the original value.
Modify the chosen field by appending ' [JH-QA-2026]' to the existing value. The marker text must be visible in the field after editing. Click the 'Save' button.

Wait for save confirmation — a success toast, 'Saved' indicator, or button state change. Verify no 500 error in the Network tab. If PATCH /api/v1/instance-config/e2e-test-instance returns non-200, record the error.

Navigate away to http://localhost:3002/cc/dashboard. Wait for dashboard to load. Navigate back to http://localhost:3002/cc/instance?instance=e2e-test-instance. Verify the edited field still contains '[JH-QA-2026]'. If the value reverted, this is a persistence failure.
Restore the original value: remove the ' [JH-QA-2026]' suffix and save. Verify the save succeeds. This cleanup ensures the live widget persona returns to its production state.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Change branding colours, save, verify widget preview reflects changes.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/instance?instance=e2e-test-instance. IMPORTANT: The instance page has multiple sub-tabs. Look for a tab bar with tabs like: 'Settings & Branding', 'Lead Form', 'Authentication', 'LLM', 'Webhooks', 'Branding'. Click the 'Branding' tab (the last one). Wait for the branding form to load.

On the Branding tab: look for colour input fields (primary colour, accent colour) and text inputs (display name, welcome message). Record the current primary colour hex value. Change it to a distinctly different value — if current is copper-ish (#c0803e), try '#10b981' (green). Enter the new hex value in the primary colour input.

Click 'Save Branding' or the save button. Check the Network tab for the request — for superadmin it should go to /api/v1/admin/instance-config/e2e-test-instance (PATCH), not /api/cc/owner/api/v1/config/branding (which is owner-only). Verify HTTP 200. A 403 means the proxy path is wrong for superadmin.
Restore the original primary colour: enter the hex value recorded in step 2 and save again. Verify the save succeeds. This prevents the live widget from showing test colours.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Flag a user, verify badge, unflag, verify removal. Validates defect #241 fix end-to-end.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/users?instance=e2e-test-instance. Wait for the users list to load. If no users exist, this journey is a SKIP (cannot test flagging without users). Record the count of flagged users (look for a 'Flagged' filter or badge count).

Select the first non-flagged user in the list. Click the 'Flag' button, flag icon, or 'Flag User' action. If a confirmation dialog appears, confirm. Verify the POST /api/v1/instance/e2e-test-instance/users/{user_id}/flag returns 200.

Verify the flagged user now shows a visual flag indicator — a badge, icon, colour change, or 'Flagged' label. Navigate to the flagged users filter or http://localhost:3002/cc/users?instance=e2e-test-instance&flagged=true. Verify the flagged user appears in the filtered view.

Unflag the user: click 'Unflag', the flag icon toggle, or 'Remove Flag'. Verify the DELETE /api/v1/instance/e2e-test-instance/users/{user_id}/flag returns 200. Verify the flag indicator is removed from the user row.
Verify the flagged users count returns to the value recorded in step 1. A user that remains flagged after unflagging, or a flagged count that does not decrement, is a persistence failure.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Check billing status page, verify tier display and usage limits.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/cc/subscription?instance=e2e-test-instance (or http://localhost:3002/cc/billing?instance=e2e-test-instance). Verify the page loads without a 500 error.
Verify a human-readable tier name is displayed — 'Free', 'Starter', 'Pro', 'Business', or similar. NOT a raw enum like 'TIER_FREE' or a UUID. Record the tier name.

Verify the monthly message or session limit is displayed as a specific number (e.g., '1,000 messages/month'). The limit must not be zero and must not be absent. A missing limit display is a UX failure.

Look for current usage alongside the limit — a progress bar, 'Used X of Y messages', or percentage. If present, verify it does not show negative numbers or values exceeding the limit. If usage display is absent, record as missing feature (soft fail).

Look for an upgrade CTA — 'Upgrade Plan', 'Get More Messages', or similar button. If found, click it. Verify it navigates to a pricing page, checkout flow, or booking link — not a 404 or blank page. Record the destination URL.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Request data export, wait for generation, verify download link.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. NOTE: The CC portal does not yet have a data-export button in the UI — this journey tests the backend API directly. First, obtain a visitor JWT: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Verify HTTP 200. Record the 'token' from the response.

Call GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/me/data-export with headers {"Authorization": "Bearer <visitor_token_from_step_1>", "X-Guide-Secret": "6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075"}. Verify HTTP 200. Verify the response body is JSON with at least one of these keys: 'profile', 'sessions', 'messages', 'conversations', or 'data'. This confirms the GDPR data export endpoint is live. NOTE: A portal UI button for self-service export is not yet implemented — flag as HALF_BUILT if the API works but the portal has no export UI.

Verify the export response contains identifiable user data: (a) the response is not empty (at least 10 bytes), (b) if a 'sessions' key exists, it is an array (possibly empty), (c) no 500 or 4xx error is returned. The test passes if the API responds with 200 and valid JSON. If the portal now has a data-export button visible, update this journey to use it instead.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Send a chat message through the widget API and verify AI response. Targets defect #225 (widget chat AI does not respond).

steps.description: Navigate to https://cc.phronex.com/ (404 on root is expected — needed for page context). Using page.evaluate(): POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with Content-Type: application/json and body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Verify HTTP 200 and response contains an access_token. Store as VISITOR_TOKEN.

Send chat message: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/chat/message with headers {"Authorization": "Bearer <VISITOR_TOKEN>", "X-Guide-Secret": "6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075", "Content-Type": "application/json"} and body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance", "message": "What does this company do?", "session_id": null}. Verify HTTP 200. If response is SSE, read until stream ends. Record the full AI response text and session_id.

Verify AI response quality: (a) at least 20 words, (b) contains relevant information about the instance's topic, (c) does NOT say 'I don\'t know' or equivalent deflection, (d) does NOT contain a stack trace, raw JSON, or internal error text. If the AI response is empty or the request returns 500, defect #225 is STILL PRESENT.

Verify session continuity: send a follow-up message in the same session — POST /api/v1/chat/message with the same session_id and message 'Tell me more'. Verify the AI remembers the previous context and does not start from scratch.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: POST /auth/anonymous returns a valid JWT with correct claims.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with Content-Type: application/json and body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Expect HTTP 200. Response shape: {"access_token": "<jwt_string>", "token_type": "bearer"}. Verify access_token is a non-empty string containing two dots (JWT format: header.payload.signature).

Decode the JWT payload (base64url decode the middle segment — do NOT verify signature, this is a contract test). Verify the payload contains: 'instance_id' = 'e2e-test-instance', 'exp' claim (expiry timestamp in the future), 'sub' or 'user_id' claim (non-empty string). If 'instance_id' is missing from claims, the token is malformed.

Verify the token works: GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/config/usage with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. Expect HTTP 200 (not 401). If 401 is returned with a valid-looking token, the auth verifier may be misconfigured for this instance.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: POST /auth/identify upgrades anonymous token to a 30-day identified session.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store the returned access_token as ANON_TOKEN.

POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/identify with Authorization: Bearer <ANON_TOKEN>, Content-Type: application/json, and body {"email": "jh-qa-identify-test@example.com", "name": "JH QA Test", "instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Expect HTTP 200. Response should contain a new access_token.

Decode the new JWT payload. Verify: (a) 'exp' claim is approximately 30 days in the future (> 25 days from now), (b) 'instance_id' = 'e2e-test-instance', (c) 'tier' field is present (any value is acceptable), (d) 'sub' field is a UUID string (CC uses UUID as subject, not email — this is correct). The 30-day expiry differentiates an identified session from the shorter anonymous session. Do NOT expect the email address in the JWT payload — CC stores user_id (UUID) as the subject.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: POST /chat/message returns SSE stream with token events.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store access_token.

POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/chat/message with headers {"Authorization": "Bearer <token>", "X-Guide-Secret": "6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075", "Content-Type": "application/json"} and body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance", "message": "Hello, what services do you offer?", "session_id": null}. Expect HTTP 200 with Content-Type: text/event-stream (SSE).

Read SSE events from the response stream. Verify: (a) at least one 'data:' line is present with a JSON payload containing a 'token' or 'text' field, (b) the stream ends with a 'done' event or closes cleanly, (c) the concatenated text forms a coherent response of at least 20 words. If the response is not SSE but a regular JSON body, verify it contains a 'response' or 'text' field.

Verify the response includes a session_id — either in the SSE metadata events, in a final JSON payload, or in response headers. The session_id is required for follow-up messages. If absent, the API contract is incomplete.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: GET /config/branding returns branding JSON with expected shape.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context for page.evaluate() calls.

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/config/branding?instance_id=e2e-test-instance').then(r=>{return {status:r.status, body:r.json()}}). Expect HTTP 200. Store response as BRANDING.

Verify BRANDING response contains: (a) 'primary_color' — a non-empty string like '#c0803e', (b) 'widget_title' or 'owner_name' — non-empty string, (c) 'welcome_message' — non-empty string. These are snake_case fields (not camelCase). Missing any field is a contract violation that breaks widget rendering.
Verify 'primary_color' matches pattern '#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}' (valid 6-digit hex). An invalid colour breaks widget rendering on customer sites. Also verify 'powered_by' is a boolean.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: GET /billing/status returns tier and limits shape.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com. Using page.evaluate(): call fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>r.json()). Verify HTTP 200 and extract access_token from response. Store as TOKEN.

Using page.evaluate() with TOKEN from step 1: call fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/billing/status', {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+TOKEN}}).then(r=>r.json()). Verify HTTP 200. Store response as BILLING.

Verify BILLING response shape: (a) 'tier' or 'plan' field is present — a string like 'free', 'starter', 'pro', (b) 'monthly_limit' or 'messages_limit' — a positive integer, (c) 'messages_used' or 'usage' — a non-negative integer. Missing tier or limit fields is a contract violation.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: POST /skills/from-template, GET /skills/{id}, DELETE /skills/{id}, verify 404 after delete.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context for API calls via page.evaluate().

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/skills/templates', {headers:{'X-Admin-Secret':'PhronexCC2025Admin'}}).then(r=>r.json()). Expect HTTP 200 with a JSON array. Verify at least one template exists. Record the first template's 'id' as TEMPLATE_ID.

Get user token first: Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>r.json()). Extract access_token as USER_TOKEN. NOTE: /skills/from-template requires user JWT (not admin secret) — it is user-scoped, not admin-scoped.

Using page.evaluate() with USER_TOKEN and TEMPLATE_ID: fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/skills/from-template', {method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+USER_TOKEN, 'Content-Type':'application/json', 'X-Guide-Secret':'6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075'}, body:JSON.stringify({template_id:TEMPLATE_ID, instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status, body:r.json()}}). Expect HTTP 201. Store the returned skill 'id' as SKILL_ID.

Using page.evaluate() with USER_TOKEN and SKILL_ID: fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/skills/'+SKILL_ID, {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+USER_TOKEN}}).then(r=>r.json()). Expect HTTP 200. Verify response contains 'id' matching SKILL_ID and 'instance_id' = 'e2e-test-instance'.

Using page.evaluate() with USER_TOKEN and SKILL_ID: fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/skills/'+SKILL_ID, {method:'DELETE', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+USER_TOKEN}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status}}). Expect HTTP 204 (no content).

Using page.evaluate() with USER_TOKEN and SKILL_ID: fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/skills/'+SKILL_ID, {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+USER_TOKEN}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status}}). Expect HTTP 404 — confirming the skill was fully deleted. A 200 response means deletion is broken.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: GET /config/usage returns messages_used and messages_remaining.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store access_token.
GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/config/usage with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Expect HTTP 200 with JSON body.

Verify response contains: (a) 'messages_used' — a non-negative integer, (b) 'messages_remaining' — a non-negative integer or null (unlimited), (c) optionally 'monthly_limit', 'reset_date'. If both messages_used and messages_remaining are absent, the usage contract is broken.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: GET /health returns {status: 'healthy', service: 'contentcompanion'}.

steps.description: GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/health. No auth required. Expect HTTP 200.

Verify response is JSON with 'status' = 'healthy' (not 'ok', not 'up'). Phronex invariant: all health endpoints return {"status": "healthy"}. Verify 'version' field is present (should be '0.1.0' or similar semver).
Also test the root health endpoint: GET https://cc.phronex.com/health. Expect HTTP 200 with the same {"status": "healthy"} shape. Both /health and /api/v1/health must return identical responses.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: GET /config/health/widget returns component health status fields.

steps.description: GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/config/health/widget?instance_id=e2e-test-instance. No auth required (public endpoint for widget self-check). Expect HTTP 200.

Verify response JSON contains component health status fields: (a) 'api' — should be 'healthy' or true, (b) 'knowledge' or 'vector_store' — status of ChromaDB, (c) 'llm' — status of Anthropic API connectivity, (d) optionally 'tts' — text-to-speech status. Each component status should be 'healthy', 'degraded', or 'unavailable'.
Verify that at least 'api' and 'llm' report 'healthy'. A degraded LLM status means Anthropic API is unreachable — this would explain defect #225 if present.

description: Layer 4 — Security: Verify admin routes reject unauthenticated requests.

steps.description: GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/users (admin users list) with NO Authorization header and NO X-Admin-Secret header. Expect HTTP 401 or 403. A 200 response means admin routes are unprotected — critical security failure.
GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/sessions (admin sessions list) with NO auth headers. Expect HTTP 401 or 403.
GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/instances (admin instance list) with NO auth headers. Expect HTTP 401 or 403.

GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/analytics (admin analytics) with NO auth headers. Expect HTTP 401 or 403. If any of these 4 admin routes return 200 without auth, record as CRITICAL SECURITY FAILURE.

description: Layer 4 — Security: Auth as instance A user, try to access instance B data.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store the access_token as INSTANCE_A_TOKEN.

Attempt cross-instance access: GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/config/usage with Authorization: Bearer <INSTANCE_A_TOKEN> and add query param ?instance_id=some-other-instance. Expect HTTP 403 or the response to only contain data for 'e2e-test-instance' (tenant isolation).

Attempt cross-instance chat: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/chat/message with Authorization: Bearer <INSTANCE_A_TOKEN> and body {"instance_id": "some-other-instance", "message": "test", "session_id": null}. Expect HTTP 403 or the server to use the token's instance_id regardless of the body's instance_id. If the server uses the body's instance_id to access a different instance's knowledge base, this is an IDOR vulnerability.

description: Layer 4 — Security: Send 25 rapid requests, verify 429 after rate limit threshold.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store access_token.

Send 25 rapid POST requests to https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/chat/message with Authorization: Bearer <token>, body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance", "message": "Hello", "session_id": null}. Do NOT wait between requests — send as fast as possible. Record the HTTP status of each response.

Analyse results: (a) if any response has status 429 — rate limiting is working, record the request number where 429 first appeared, (b) if all 25 return 200 — rate limit threshold is > 25 or rate limiting is disabled, record as 'rate limit not triggered in 25 requests' (conditional pass), (c) if any response is 500 — server crashed under load, record as HARD FAIL.

If 429 was received: verify the response body contains a human-readable message field (e.g., 'Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.'). A raw {"detail": "rate_limit_exceeded"} with no user-friendly message is a UX failure.

description: Layer 4 — Security: Send requests with malformed JWT tokens, verify 401 responses.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context for page.evaluate() calls.

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/billing/status', {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer TRUNCATED_TOKEN_ABC123'}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status}}). Expect HTTP 401 or 422 (not 500). 401=missing/invalid JWT, 422=validation error before auth. A 500 means JWT decoding throws unhandled exception. PASS on any non-500 response.

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/billing/status', {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJ0ZXN0In0.INVALID_SIGNATURE_HERE'}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status}}). Expect HTTP 401. Invalid signature must be rejected.
Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/billing/status', {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status}}). Expect HTTP 401.

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/billing/status', {headers:{'Authorization':'InvalidScheme abc123'}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status}}). Expect HTTP 401 or 422. Never 500.

description: Layer 4 — Security: Send script tag payload in chat message, verify response is escaped/safe.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context. Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>r.json()). Extract access_token. Store as TOKEN.

Using page.evaluate() with TOKEN: fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/chat/message', {method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+TOKEN, 'Content-Type':'application/json', 'X-Guide-Secret':'6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075'},body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:'e2e-test-instance', message:' Tell me about Phronex. ', session_id:null})}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status, text:r.text()}}). Expect HTTP 200. Record response text as RESPONSE.

Verify RESPONSE text does NOT contain unescaped '<script>' tags or 'onerror=' attributes that would execute JavaScript. The AI's response should discuss the question normally. Pass if: response is 200 AND the response body is plain text/JSON without raw HTML script injection. Fail if: response body echoes back '<script>alert(1)</script>' as literal HTML.

description: Layer 4 — Security: Send SQL injection payload in auth identify email, verify no error leak.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context for page.evaluate() calls.

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>r.json()). Extract access_token. Store as TOKEN.

Using page.evaluate() with TOKEN: fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/identify', {method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+TOKEN, 'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({email:"test@example.com' OR '1'='1", name:'SQLi Test', instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status, text:r.text()}}). Expect HTTP 422 or 400 (validation error). NOT 500 (which would indicate a SQL error leaked).

Verify the response from step 2 does NOT contain SQL error messages: no 'syntax error', no 'pg_catalog', no 'relation', no 'column', no PostgreSQL error codes. A clean 422 or 400 validation error is passing. A 500 with SQL error text is a FAIL.

Using page.evaluate() with TOKEN: fetch('https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/identify', {method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+TOKEN, 'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({email:"'; DROP TABLE users; --", name:'SQLi Test', instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status, text:r.text()}}). Expect 422 or 400. Verify no SQL errors in response.

description: Layer 4 — Security: Verify admin routes require X-Admin-Secret header.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context.
Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context for subsequent API calls via page.evaluate().
Using page.evaluate(): fetch('cc.phronex.com/api/v1/users with X-Admin-Secret: wrong-secret-value. Expect HTTP 401 or 403. If the response is 200, the admin secret validation is broken.
Using page.evaluate(): fetch('cc.phronex.com/api/v1/instances with X-Admin-Secret: (empty string). Expect HTTP 401 or 403.

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('POST:https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/ip-blocks with X-Admin-Secret: wrong-secret and body {"ip": "192.0.2.1", "reason": "test"}. Expect HTTP 401 or 403. An IP block created with a wrong secret is a critical auth bypass.

description: Layer 5 — Business Logic: Verify free tier monthly message limit is enforced.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store access_token.

GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/billing/status with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Record the 'tier' value and 'monthly_limit' value. For a free tier, the monthly_limit should be a positive integer (e.g., 20, 50, 100).

GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/config/usage with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Record 'messages_used' and 'messages_remaining'. Verify: messages_used + messages_remaining = monthly_limit (or close, allowing for concurrent usage). If messages_remaining is null or absent, the limit enforcement is not functional.

Verify tier configuration matches expectations: free tier monthly_limit should be between 10 and 200 messages. If monthly_limit is 0 or > 10000, the tier config is likely wrong. Record the exact values for comparison with premium tier.

description: Layer 5 — Business Logic: Verify premium users get higher limits and premium-only features.

steps.description: GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/admin/instance-config/e2e-test-instance with X-Admin-Secret: PhronexCC2025Admin header. NOTE: Use /admin/instance-config/{id} — NOT /instance/{id}/tiers which requires owner JWT. Expect HTTP 200. Extract the 'tiers' key from the response — it is a JSON object whose keys are tier names (e.g. 'free', 'premium'). Record the tier names and their monthly_limit values.

Verify tier hierarchy: (a) at least 2 tiers exist (free + one paid), (b) each paid tier has a higher monthly_limit than free, (c) tier names are human-readable strings. If only one tier exists, premium features cannot be verified.

Check for premium-only features by examining tier config: look for fields like 'custom_branding', 'priority_support', 'advanced_analytics', 'custom_skills', 'tts_enabled' that differ between tiers. Record which features are gated to premium tiers.

description: Layer 5 — Business Logic: POST /billing/checkout returns Razorpay subscription_id and checkout URL.

steps.description: POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store access_token.

POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/billing/checkout with Authorization: Bearer <token>, Content-Type: application/json, and body {"tier": "pro"} (or the first paid tier name from cc-biz-premium-features). Expect HTTP 200 or 201.

Verify response contains: (a) 'subscription_id' — a Razorpay subscription ID string starting with 'sub_', (b) 'checkout_url' or 'short_url' — a valid URL containing 'razorpay.com'. If Razorpay is not configured (key_id missing), expect HTTP 503 or 400 with an informative error — not a 500 crash.

If checkout succeeded: verify the subscription_id format matches Razorpay's pattern (sub_[a-zA-Z0-9]+). Do NOT follow the checkout URL — it would create a real billing session. If the response is a 400/503 with 'billing not configured', record as expected for test instances without Razorpay keys.

description: Layer 5 — Business Logic: Compare rate limits between tiers, verify premium gets higher limits.

steps.description: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com to establish browser context for API calls.

GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/admin/instance-config/e2e-test-instance with X-Admin-Secret: PhronexCC2025Admin header. NOTE: Use /admin/instance-config/{id} (admin-secret auth) — NOT /instance/{id}/tiers which requires owner JWT. Extract the 'tiers' object from the response. Record each tier's monthly_limit and rate_limit_hourly values.

Verify rate limit ordering: premium tiers must have rate_limit_hourly >= free tier's rate_limit_hourly. If all tiers have the same rate limit, record as 'no rate differentiation by tier' — the RATE_LIMIT_HOURLY env var may be a global ceiling.

Verify monthly limit ordering: each successive tier must have monthly_limit >= the previous tier. Free < Starter < Pro < Business (or equivalent). If a higher tier has fewer monthly messages than a lower tier, this is a configuration error.

description: Layer 5 — Business Logic: When LLM is unavailable, verify /chat/message returns graceful error.

steps.description: GET https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/config/health/widget?instance_id=e2e-test-instance. Check the 'llm' component status. If 'llm' is 'unavailable' or 'degraded', proceed to verify graceful error handling. If 'llm' is 'healthy', this test verifies the API contract shape only (cannot force LLM unavailability in production).

POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/auth/anonymous with body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance"}. Store token. POST https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/chat/message with the token and body {"instance_id": "e2e-test-instance", "message": "test", "session_id": null}.

If LLM is healthy: verify 200 with a valid response (baseline check). If LLM is unavailable: verify the response is NOT a 500 with a stack trace — it should be a 503 with a user-friendly message like 'The AI assistant is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.' A raw exception in the response body violates the 'fail safe' principle.
